item.title: Installation
item.description:
Requirements

  • PHP 7.4 or newer with the pdo_sqlite and mbstring extensions (and curl if you use webhooks or the RSS extension).
  • A modern browser.

There is nothing to compile or install.

Run it

Download or clone the repository, then start PHP’s built-in server in that folder:

git clone https://github.com/andjar/notd.git
cd notd
php -S localhost:8000

Open http://localhost:8000. The database is created on first use and today’s journal page opens with a few welcome notes.

item.title: Core Concepts
item.description:
Pages

A page is a named container of notes. Names are unique and case-insensitive.

  • Journal pages are named after a date (2026-11-10) and are created the first time you open that date.
  • Namespaces. A / in the name creates a hierarchy: Projects/Alpha is a child of Projects, and each page lists its children.
  • A page has its own content for page-level properties, edited through the gear icon next to the title.

Notes

A note is one bullet in the outline: a piece of Markdown that belongs to a page and optionally to a parent note. Notes have a stable id, which you can use to link to a note (page.php?page=Name#note-<id>) or to embed it elsewhere.

item.title: Changelog
item.description:
November 2026: schema v3

Upgrading needs one command: php db/migrate_v3.php (see Installation).

Saving

  • All note changes go through one endpoint, ops.php, which applies a batch of operations atomically and can be retried safely. notes.php is read-only and the old batch endpoint is gone.
  • Notes get their permanent id (a UUIDv7) in the browser. Temporary ids are gone, so Enter followed by Tab, typing on a slow connection and attaching a file to a new note all work.
  • Siblings are ordered by fractional keys: moving a note rewrites one row. This fixes reordering that corrupted the order of unrelated notes.
  • Edits are queued in the browser, survive reloads and offline periods, and other open tabs follow along.
  • Ctrl/Alt+Shift + Up/Down move a note among its siblings.

Security and robustness
